reason: The cited evidence (E2) shows that vacuum heat treatment at 500 °C improves room-temperature wear resistance and microhardness for different coatings, but it does not address FeNiCrCoCu, high-temperature wear, oxide layer formation, or microstructural refinement mechanisms. E1 is entirely about a different alloy and property. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Vacuum heat treatment at ~500 °C refines the near-surface microstructure of FeNiCrCoCu coatings (stabilizing grain boundaries, promoting nanostructural features).
Vacuum heat treatment at ~500 °C promotes the formation of a thin, adherent oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Microstructural refinement and oxide layer formation together increase hardness.
Increased hardness and oxide layer reduce both abrasive and adhesive wear at high temperature.
These effects are operative and dominant under high-temperature sliding (500–700 °C) and high loads.
